newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Wool Exchange changes pack standard.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Wool Exchange changes pack standard.

text.p: The Australian Wool Exchange Ltd said on Tuesday it will phase out its Standard 1 wool packs from July 1, 1997 to fight the contamination in processed wool.
Packs already in circulation will still be acceptable, but will cease to become available as for retail sale as stocks dry up, it said.

Standard 1 packs are to be replaced by Standard 5 packs, which the exchange said represented "a positive step, which has been taken now to reduce contamination from packs, which would not add significant costs to woolgrowers at a time of hardship."
Standard 5 packs cost about A$1.00 more each than Standard 1, the exchange said. Each Standard 1 packs costs about A$8.00.
The price difference between the two packs should drop as more manufacturers switch to Standard 5 production, it said.
The exchange also said it will continue to encourage the use of nylon and other "non-contaminating" packs, particularly for finer combing wool.

"Statistical analysis undertaken by the Wool Exchange shows a premium of 50 cents a kg/clean being paid for wool packed in nylon (styles MF3, 4,5 and 17 to 19m) and it is hoped that in time, if mills preference wool in nylon packs in their orders, this premium will extend to coarser microns," the exchange said.

The decision to switch packs follows complaints by some wool processors about conatimnation from the packs, Dennis Teasdale, national manager of quality assurance for the exchange, told Reuters. "We see this as a modest step," Teasdale said.
A study by the exchange based on a survey of the causes of contamination estimated that 30 percent of contamination problems were related to packaging, he said.
